newsitem.title: UK: Man sees world 96/97 sugar output at 122.72 mln t.
newsitem.headline: Man sees world 96/97 sugar output at 122.72 mln t.

text.p: World 1996/997 (crop year) sugar output will total 122.722 million tonnes, according to a report released by international trade house E D & F Man.
The previous year's output was 123,531 million tonnes. Both figures are based on raw value.
The world's surplus of sugar will be 2.43 million tonnes, compared with a previous year figure of 5.15 million.

In its February report, Man said that the bulk of the cut in its output forecast, from a previous estimate of 123.54 million tonnes was accounted for by India, where the crop outlook has changed quite dramatically in recent months. India has a huge influence, as the largest single producer of cane sugar, Man said.
Indian production for 1996/07 is now put at 14.348 million tonnes, compared with the previous year's figure of 17.883 million, both figures on a raw value basis.
Estimates for European sugar output "have undergone a radical upward revision, following the late surge in beet sugar content among the leading west European producers," Man said.

In the EU alone, Man's estimate has increased by almost 1.1 million tonnes white value to stand at 16.43 million tonnes. It puts EU 1996/97 production at 17.861 million tonnes raw value. "With the sole exception of Finland, all our EU production estimates have been increased since September," Man said.
